short: Overt-to-covert EEG transfer (M04) is not new, even on this dataset; the overt-only control is missing, the from-scratch baseline is unmatched, and 79.82% is tied to no fine-tuning fraction.
position: The paper [@duraisamy2025transfer] changes the use-time action (M04, with M01 and M03): a BiLSTM trained on a person's overt-speech EEG is frozen and its output layer re-trained on 15-30% of that person's covert trials; Table II gives 79.82% on five commands against 66.94% from scratch, but not which fraction yields it. Its claim that no one had transferred an overt classifier to imagined speech is wrong: Lee et al. did so in EEG with five words [@lee2023spoken], and the paper's own dataset study did so on these recordings, 61.78% against 71.48% for silent training [@rekrut2022improving]. M04 is not reported: the overt-only condition both studies report is missing, so pretraining is not separated from covert fine-tuning. The 12.88-point gain (inference) is also confounded with an unstated from-scratch data amount and a within-person split. The features and BiLSTM (M06) are standard and never ablated.
